subject: mcc-acute-care
title: Psychiatric emergencies: recognising and acting fast

steps.tx: Psychiatric emergencies are presentations where a patient is a danger to self or others, or has a medical or drug-induced condition that threatens life. Many look like psychiatry but are medical, so always check vital signs, glucose and drug exposure. A **toxidrome** or **drug reaction** should be considered first. Assessment must be quick, structured and documented.

steps.tx: Drug-induced syndromes need rapid recognition. **Neuroleptic malignant syndrome** presents with fever, rigidity, reduced consciousness and raised creatine kinase, usually days after starting or raising an antipsychotic. **Serotonin toxicity** presents with clonus, agitation and hyperthermia, often within hours to days of adding a second serotonergic drug. Both need the offending drug stopped and supportive care.

steps.tx: Acute dystonia occurs within hours of a dopamine blocker such as intramuscular haloperidol. It causes sustained neck torsion or fixed gaze, and it is not dangerous to life. **Anticholinergic** drugs such as benztropine relieve it quickly. Lithium toxicity is different: coarse tremor, vomiting and confusion in a patient on lithium with a thiazide or volume loss need urgent serum lithium, renal function and IV saline.

left.title: Acute dystonia
points: Onset within hours of dopamine blocker
Treat with benztropine IV or IM

right.title: Lithium toxicity
points: Raised level with low sodium or high creatinine
Stop lithium and give IV saline
Dialysis when severe or renal failure

steps.tx: Drug-induced QT prolongation and **torsades de pointes** can be fatal. Antipsychotics, macrolides, citalopram and other agents block cardiac potassium channels. Check ECG, potassium and magnesium, and remove offending drugs. Continuous cardiac monitoring is needed when QT is prolonged or after significant overdose. Acetaminophen overdose needs N-acetylcysteine without waiting for a level when ingestion time is unknown.

steps.tx: Capacity and risk decide the pathway. Assess whether the patient can understand, retain, weigh and communicate a decision. A relative is not a legal substitute decision-maker in every case. Involuntary care is allowed only when the criteria in the provincial mental health legislation are met. A patient with a specific plan to die, a recent self-harm act or firearm access is high risk and needs **continuous observation** and urgent psychiatric assessment.

nodes.label: Least restrictive care or involuntary criteria

steps.tx: Across these scenarios, start by excluding a **medical cause**, such as delirium, intoxication or hypoglycaemia. Next, secure **safety** and complete a structured **risk assessment**. Patients with low risk and intact **capacity** may be discharged with a written safety plan and early follow-up. Those at high risk need observation and **psychiatry review** before any move. Document your reasoning, and repeat vital signs and drug levels as the picture changes.
steps.say: In every one of these scenarios, begin by ruling out a medical cause, for example delirium, intoxication or low blood sugar. Then make sure the patient is safe and carry out a structured risk assessment. Patients who are low risk and have intact capacity may go home with a written safety plan and early follow-up. Those at high risk need observation and a psychiatry review before any move. Record your reasoning clearly, and repeat vital signs and drug levels as the clinical picture changes.
